primary_number: Q5 richest quintile: per-inpatient-episode OOP = IDR 2,699,500 (~USD 173); per-outpatient-episode OOP = IDR 335,500 (~USD 22). National average annual OOP per capita = IDR 447,000-651,000 (USD 31-42). Q5 urban annual OOP per capita estimated IDR 976,000-1,302,000 (USD 63-83) based on 1.5-2x national average scaling — no direct quintile-level annual figure found in open-access sources.
publisher: International Journal for Equity in Health (Fattah et al. 2023) — ENHANCE Household Panel Study 2018-2019, Indonesia
methodology_note: PMC10483778 (DOI: 10.1186/s12939-023-01980-w) reports per-episode OOP by wealth quintile from the ENHANCE Household Panel Study 2018-2019, a nationally representative survey. Table 2 provides outpatient and inpatient OOP conditional on utilization. Annual per-capita OOP is NOT directly reported by quintile. National average annual household OOP = IDR 743,773 (USD 53) from Susenas 2018-2019 cross-sectional data (PLOS Global Public Health, DOI: 10.1371/journal.pgph.0000203). WHO NHA Indonesia 2024 reports total health expenditure per capita of IDR 2.3M with OOP share = 28.3%, implying national OOP per capita of ~IDR 651,000 (USD 42 at IDR 15,600). Q5 urban annual figure requires scaling: Q5 monthly household expenditure was IDR 6,664,000 vs estimated national average ~IDR 4,500,000, a ratio of ~1.48x. Applying 1.5-2x multiplier to national OOP per capita yields IDR 976K-1.3M per capita per year for Q5. Private health benefit incidence is pro-rich (Lancet Global Health 2023, concentration index 0.134-0.190), supporting higher Q5 OOP but no direct quintile-annual figure found.
health_education_split: NOT EVIDENCED. No open-access primary source found providing the health (kesehatan) vs education (pendidikan) breakdown as shares of combined social spend at top deciles from BPS Susenas BUKLE tables. BPS Health Statistics Profile 2023 and the main Susenas 2023 expenditure publication both returned HTTP 403 (access restricted). The 50/50 assumption in the skill draft remains unverified. All available papers (PMC10483778, PLOS GPH JKN study, Lancet Global Health 2023 benefit incidence study) focus on health OOP only, not the health-education composition of non-food expenditure at the decile level. BPS Silastik microdata access would be required to verify this split.
